messages:
liz: quick thought — as we prep the v3->v4 cutover we should formalize a compatibility playbook. not just a shim, but guardrails: where shims live, eviction policy, and the telemetry signals to auto-triage regressions. thoughts? :thinking:
amar: strong agree. runtime shims for tiny shape differences (headers/envelope), separate adapter for heavier changes. keeps hotpath lean.
sasha: also need SDK behavior. if we rely only on server shims customers will get surprised. short-term SDKs should emit deprecation warnings when they detect legacy shapes.
kevin: what exact signals do we need? % requests routed to shim, error-rate delta for v4 opt-ins, latency delta, and per-tenant regression score.
olivia (pm): those are good. also a TTL policy: shims auto-expire after N months unless product requests extension. and a "no silent removals" rule for any field deletion.
liz: concrete proposal: 1) header semantics: `X-RI-Compat: v3` routes to compat layer; missing header => v4 by default. 2) shim placement: edge proxy for routing + idempotent lightweight translations, runtime for KV-cache and tokenization fallbacks. 3) telemetry tags like `ri.compat.v3` and `ri.compat.translation=header|body|proto`.
amar: ops notes: (a) edge translations must be idempotent so retries don't multiply effects, (b) runtime shims should avoid copies — use views/mapped buffers.
sasha: SDK plan: add `Client.enableCompat('v3')` that sets the header; SDKs should also log a local deprecation message linking to the migration docs. ship in next minor, mark in changelog.
kevin: add a daily job that scans shimmed traffic for quality regressions (evals + recorded prompts) and auto-open an incident if deltas exceed thresholds.
olivia (pm): private deployments: need tenant-level toggle (e.g., `compat_enabled: true|false`) so infra can control defaults.
liz: precedence: tenant flag overrides global default, header overrides tenant flag (explicit opt-in/out). global admin can force v4 for safety.
amar: rollout technique: dark-launch canary where 1% of v3 traffic is translated by v4 path to surface silent regressions.
sasha: testing matrix: unit tests for translations, integration tests exercising edge+runtime paths, and a nightly compat eval suite (`tests/compat/`) using anonymized customer prompts. KV-cache integrity checks required.
kevin: perf budget per shim: avg <10ms overhead, p95 <40ms. mark shim "expensive" if above and require opt-in.
olivia (pm): timeline: RFC + prototype this sprint, canary next sprint, tenant opt-in over 6-8 weeks, migration docs + deprecation notice week 10, full sunset only after 3 months with zero active opt-ins.
liz: header format idea: `X-RI-Compat: v3;reason=client_sdk;ts=1670000000`. add `X-RI-Compat-Debug: 1` for verbose traces in support mode.
amar: implementation: small library `redwood/compat/v3` exposing pure `normalize_request(req) -> req'` and `normalize_response(res) -> res'`. no side effects. SDKs can vendor minimal helpers if needed.
kevin: telemetry naming: use dotted metric keys `ri.compat.v3.*` to fit ingestion rules. also avoid logging raw payloads in debug traces; prefer shape hashes + masked samples and a consent toggle for private tenants.
sasha: sample user warning: "You're using a legacy request shape — please migrate. Docs: https://redwood.dev/migrate-v4". include quick remediation steps in SDK warning.
olivia (pm): I'll draft the customer-facing migration slug `v4-inference-api-migration` and start docs outline.
liz: next actions: amar -> shim placement diagram, sasha -> SDK flag + warning text, kevin -> telemetry thresholds & perf budgets, olivia -> migration comms + timeline. I'll assemble RFC PR by EOD Friday.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: compat-shim-prototype -> staging @4201236600 :rocket:
kevin: quick Q — should debug traces include original payload? privacy concerns. prefer hash + sanitized shape only.
amar: agreed. hash + schema fingerprint + masked sample values. add tenant consent toggle for richer traces.
sasha: +1 :thumbsup: will add short example and migration link in the warning.
olivia (pm): this is a good, non-ad-hoc approach. I'll follow up with the RFC PR.
liz: merging notes for RFC checklist: rollout plan, telemetry thresholds, perf budgets, SDK releases, tenant flag behavior, sunset policy, testing matrix. archive this thread for traceability. :white_check_mark:
